items.title: Loop vs Graph Engineering Clearly Explained
items.excerpt: A short commentary clarifying that a loop is a 1-node graph and reaching for a multi-node graph too early adds complexity without fixing a broken loop.
items.body: In July 2026, Twitter debated whether loop engineering was dead in favor of graph engineering. A loop is simply a 1-node graph. Only split into multiple nodes when work genuinely needs parallel tracks or isolated context. Subscribe to my newsletter for a full roadmap.

items.title: How the Claude Code Team Thinks About Verification
items.excerpt: When ~90% of code is written and reviewed by AI agents, human engineering shifts to defining done, E2E/property/differential tests, base-branch REVIEW.md, diff-triggered checklists, 3-strike escalation, observe->enforce commit gates, and empirical reviewer evals.
items.body: Roughly 90% of Claude Code's code is written and reviewed by Claude. Invest in 3 un-gameable test types: E2E runtime tests via CDP/MCP, property-based tests (fast-check/Hypothesis/proptest), and differential tests. Always load REVIEW.md from the base branch (never PR head), attach diff-readable triggers to reliability checklists (39 items, running only the 3-10 matching checks), enforce 3-strike human escalation, roll out commit verification gates via off->observe->enforce with a 2-block escape hatch, and evaluate review rules empirically against reverted PRs and size-matched clean controls.

items.title: Harness, Loop, Graph: The 3 Layers That Decide If Your AI Agent Works
items.excerpt: Environment, then feedback, then flow. Collapse agent infrastructure into Harness (contract, map, <=10 tools, disk memory, walls, traces), Loop (deterministic evidence, EXPECTED vs SAW, same-result-twice exit), and Graph (Early-Start Test, 4 Cuts) plus Undo-Price Gating.
items.body: Stop fixing agent failures by rewriting prompts. Layer 1 Harness defines done_when, short AGENTS.md map, <=10 narrow tools, disk memory, external walls, and Write It Twice (prose GUIDE + CI CHECK). Layer 2 Loop runs deterministic evidence, emits EXPECTED vs SAW, and breaks on retry cap or same-result-twice. Layer 3 Graph applies the Early-Start Test and 4 Cuts (use deterministic code when output should never vary; freeze passed nodes). Gate risk by undo price: ONE-CLICK UNDO, CLEANUP UNDO, NO UNDO.

items.title: v2.1.323 — Experimental Code Mode Programmatic Tool Execution
items.excerpt: Launches experimental Code Mode (CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE=1) executing generated JS scripts across Bash/Read/Edit/MCP outside the context window, with interactive-CLI-only, HIPAA/ZDR/Bedrock blocks, and PreToolUse tool_input.code hook caveats.
items.body: Adds experimental Code Mode in Claude Code v2.1.323+. Instead of sequential tool calls that bloat context with raw MCP outputs, Claude writes a single JS script executed in a local REPL returning only distilled summaries. Caveats: interactive CLI only (no -p, SDK, IDE, cloud), incompatible with Agent Teams, blocked under HIPAA/ZDR/Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry, and naive PreToolUse Bash hooks miss wrapped commands unless inspecting tool_input.code.

items.title: Choosing a Claude Model and Tuning Reasoning Effort
items.excerpt: Separate model capability ceiling from thinking effort dial (low->max), tune effort before upgrading models, avoid mid-session effort toggles that invalidate prompt caches, and delegate mechanical subagents down the cost curve.
items.body: Two orthogonal dials govern agent economics: Model Tier sets the frozen capability ceiling while Effort controls dynamic thinking compute. Turn effort down when a model over-engineers simple tasks and up one notch when it rushes—before switching models. Avoid toggling effort mid-session because it can invalidate prompt caches; pair tier switches with clean phase boundaries.

items.title: Andrej Karpathy: ASD-STE100 (STE-80) and The 4-Level Understanding Ladder
items.excerpt: Use ~80% of ASD-STE100 controlled English (one term per concept, condition-first, <=20-25 words per sentence) and escalate up the 4-level understanding ladder: STE-80 text -> diagrams -> discardable interactive HTML -> procedural animations.
items.body: As models take on autonomous work, human work shifts to oversight and comprehension. Default LLM prose rotates synonyms and buries actions in compound sentences. Prompt for ~80% ASD-STE100 (STE-80) and apply STE structural rules to AGENTS.md and SKILL.md with a deterministic linter. Escalate output modality across 4 levels: (1) STE-80 controlled text, (2) Mermaid/SVG diagrams, (3) throwaway interactive HTML widgets, (4) 3b1b-style procedural explainer animations. Guard against authority bias by requiring execution evidence and UNCONFIRMED tags.
